headline: Oil bounces back after attacks on Saudi refineries and tankers, days before OPEC+ meets.
summary: Oil rose again this week. Attacks hit two Saudi refineries and tankers near Iran. It is still well below October's $125 average. India's harvests are shrinking after a dry monsoon. That keeps rice and wheat in focus. The US also proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and India.
lookback: Gold and silver kept falling, as the last read expected. Gold hit its lowest price in more than a year. Oil did not keep slipping, though. It bounced back after new attacks on Saudi refineries and tankers. India has not decided on its rice tax yet. But its own harvest estimate now shows less rice and much less maize. We found no new Russian wheat rules. OPEC+ and the FAO's November food prices are still ahead.

items.title: Oil bounces back as attacks hit Saudi refineries and tankers
items.text: Brent crude (the main world oil price) was near $97 a barrel on Friday, Interfax reported. The Houthis (a Yemeni armed group) hit Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery. A day later, a refinery in Jazan was hit, killing a worker. Iran also said two more tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Oil is still below October's $125 average. OPEC+ (the big oil countries' group) meets on Sunday. Bloomberg says it may keep output limits unchanged for January. More attacks could push gas prices back up.

items.title: India's harvests shrink after a weak monsoon
items.text: India now expects its summer grain harvest to be about 5% smaller than last year. Rice is down about 2%, and maize about 15%. A weak monsoon (the summer rainy season) caused it. Winter planting is lagging too: wheat fields are 17% smaller so far, as soils are dry. Rice in Indian shops cost 12.5% more in October than a year before. India has a lot of rice in storage, but not the kinds people want most. World rice and wheat were both 37% pricier in October than a year before. Smaller Indian harvests make limits on sales abroad more likely.

items.title: US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, China hit hardest
items.text: The US proposed new tariffs (taxes on goods coming in) on 14 trading partners on Wednesday. They include China, the EU, India and Indonesia. China would face an extra 20%, the highest rate. China rejected the US claims. The US also plans higher duties on Brazilian sugar above a set amount. A US-China trade truce ends on 10 January. If talks go well, the tariffs could shrink. If they fail, China could buy fewer US crops, as it did before. Tariffs can also raise prices for shoppers.

items.title: El Niño adds new hunger hotspots, the UN warns
items.text: El Niño (the Pacific running warm) pushed Southern Africa and Central America onto the UN's hunger hotspot list. The FAO (the UN's food agency) and the WFP (its food aid agency) said so on Friday. Hotter, drier weather threatens planting in Zimbabwe, Malawi and Mozambique. In Central America, the first crop season was the driest in 40 years. The list now has 16 places, up from 13 in June. Sudan and South Sudan are at risk of famine. When harvests fail, these countries must buy more food abroad.

items.title: Gold falls to its lowest in over a year on rate-rise bets
items.text: Gold fell more than 3% on Wednesday, to its lowest price in over a year. Silver slipped to about $41 an ounce. Traders see a 95% chance that the Fed (the US central bank) raises interest rates on 8-9 December. Higher rates make gold, which pays no interest, less attractive. US inflation data that day also came in firm. Gold was $4,105 an ounce on average in October, 13% below its high of the past six months.

checked.note: Brent rose to near $97 after Houthi hits on two Saudi refineries; OPEC+ meets Sunday.
Gazprom expects gas prices to keep rising once the EU bans Russian LNG on 1 Jan. No big urea news.
FAO and WFP say El Niño is gaining strength and added new hunger hotspots. NOAA blocked; next update due in December.
Palm oil rose about 2% on the week; Indonesia's export agency proposed a 0.5% fee. Malaysia's exports dipped.
India's summer grain estimate fell 5%; wheat planting is 17% behind. No rice tax decision yet.
Russia banned buckwheat sales abroad for six months (27 Nov). No new wheat rule or quota found.
US plans higher duties on Brazilian sugar. No new soybean or maize crop news reached (CONAB blocked).
IGC (20 Nov) raised its Australian grain forecast. No newer Australian wheat news could be opened.
US proposes an extra 20% tariff on China; China rejects it. Their trade truce ends 10 Jan.
FAO and WFP list 16 hunger hotspots, adding Southern Africa and Chad. Sudan and South Sudan risk famine.
Iran says two more tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz; Houthis hit Saudi Red Sea ports.
FAO-WFP Hunger Hotspots report out 27 Nov. FAO and USDA sites blocked; no other new report found.
Gold fell to its lowest in over a year; silver near $41; copper fell about 4% in one day.
Traders see a 95% chance of a Fed hike on 8-9 Dec. South Korea's central bank raised rates.
US proposed new tariffs on 14 partners. Report says US urged Iraq and Venezuela to leave OPEC.
